content: A husband claimed a full refund for a house purchase and its renovation, citing the use of personal funds from selling his own pre-marital properties,. The court had to differentiate between purchase reimbursements and investment reimbursements under Articles 192 and 194,. The judge ruled that funds used for the initial purchase of a common asset are not refundable due to the principle of parity,. However, personal funds proven to have been spent specifically on renovations or improvements to a shared asset are reimbursable as "investments" in the common heritage.
